presentation.purpose: Reorganize dimensions while keeping every number in reading order.

learning.title: Explore Reshape in a classifier
learning.subtitle: Reorganize dimensions while keeping every number in reading order.
learning.formula: Reshape changes how numbers are grouped into rows and columns. It does not move numbers out of reading order or calculate new values.
paragraphs: Add Reshape from Tensor layout, then choose Set dimensions. Each grid row describes one sample dimension; use Infer for at most one automatically calculated size. The batch N stays separate.

Use the arrows to order dimensions and Add dimension to extend the grid. Planned shape uses declared input metadata; it is not captured execution data. Apply only when the requested dimensions hold exactly the same values.
Choose Flatten axes on the same component to combine consecutive sample directions. The editable example and original Tensor layout lab exercises retain their saved Reshape and Flatten identities.

presentation.purpose: Exchange two directions while preserving the matching values.

learning.title: Explore Transpose in a classifier
learning.subtitle: Exchange two directions while preserving the matching values.
learning.formula: Transpose exchanges two directions in an array. For a table, rows become columns.
paragraphs: Add Transpose and choose Swap axes. Select two sample axes; known input sizes appear beside their axis numbers. Negative axes count from the end, and batch N remains separate.
Apply swaps the two directions without changing the values. Planned shapes use declared metadata; Results shows captured tensors after execution.
Reorder axes is the same placement’s full-permutation mode. Original Transpose and Permute projects, examples and assessed lessons retain their identities.

presentation.purpose: Combine consecutive directions into a longer row of values.

learning.title: Explore Flatten in a classifier
learning.subtitle: Combine consecutive directions into a longer row of values.
learning.formula: Flatten joins a consecutive range of sample directions. It keeps the values in logical reading order.
paragraphs: Add Reshape from Tensor layout and choose Flatten axes. Start axis and End axis choose the inclusive range to combine. Negative numbers count from the end; −1 remains the last sample axis as rank changes.

Keep batch N separate. Flatten can combine just part of a tensor; dimensions outside the selected range remain. Planned shape uses declared input metadata, while Results contains only captured values.
Original Flatten projects and lab exercises open in the same inspector without changing their behavior. Switch to Set dimensions only when you want an explicit ordered dimension grid, then Apply.
